comment: The game's GroundEffectTypes table, vendored so a patch of ground can be NAMED and JUDGED without a Path of Exile install. The GroundEffect component carries only a row index (+0x48); this turns it into the game's own name, the buff that kind applies, the sentence the player reads while standing in it, and whether it hurts. HOW harm IS DECIDED, stated because it is a judgement and every judgement here should be inspectable - the why field carries it per row. It comes from BuffDefinitions.BuffCategory: category 2 is the debuff categories and every one of those rows describes itself as damage, a slow or a drain; category 1 grants something; category 18 is invisible and carries no description at all, and where such a row is one of the named ailment grounds (ignited, chilled, shocked, scorched, brittle, sapped, withered, quicksand, poison) it is harmful because the ailment is. Anything left is UNCLEAR rather than guessed: Smoke and the row literally called Unused say nothing, and Leyline cuts both ways - more spell damage while it drains your Ward. 44 harmful, 6 helpful, 3 unclear. WHY VENDORED WHEN THE INSTALL IS AUTHORITATIVE: without it the feature is dead on a machine that only replays a recording - which is every machine this project's tests run on - so the resolution could not be tested at all, only its failure modes. GroundEffectTypeTable prefers the install for the name and always takes harm and the description from here, because the install carries neither without a second and third table. A row this file does not know is reported as its number, never guessed. NOTE THAT HARM IS ABOUT THE TYPE, NOT THE MOMENT: an expired patch still reports harmful, which is correct - the countdown is what says whether it is still burning.
